transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-02 Start: 09:23 PST Duration: 48 minutes Attendees: Ari Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Nguyen (Elmwood - Head of Vendor Risk), Tom Hayes (Elmwood - Security Engineer), Priya Sharma (Elmwood - Procurement)

Summary: Quick alignment on SIG/CAIQ completion strategy, evidence packaging, and technical follow-ups for KMS/encryption and data residency. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: SIG strategy, SOC 2 / ISO scoping, KMS & encryption, audit logs export, data residency and VPC/private deployment, evidence packaging, timeline for procurement.

00:00 Ari Chen: Hi everyone thanks for joining early like we said we'll try to keep this to about 45ish minutes uh just quick intros on both sides
00:08 Rachel Nguyen: Hi I'm Rachel, head of vendor risk at Elmwood, thanks Ari
00:12 Tom Hayes: Tom here, focus on infra and security engineering, will be deep into KMS and logs
00:17 Priya Sharma: Priya from procurement, watching timelines and contract stuff
00:22 Ari Chen: Great, hey Samira do you want to outline the SIG/CAIQ approach and the evidence bundle we typically share
00:30 Samira Patel: Yeah sure, so typically we start with the SIG baseline answers, we map each control to the supporting artifact, e.g., SOC 2 Type II report, dataflow diagrams, encryption key management notes. We'll highlight where Redwood runs in our hosted env vs dedicated/private options. Note, sometimes the automated transcriber writes KMS as K-M-S or kms, so just flag that. Uh, we'll also flag any controls that need additional attestation, like data residency or air-gapped on-prem.
01:00 Rachel Nguyen: For Elmwood we have two blockers: data residency for EU clients and proof of key separation for certain funds, and we also need to know audit log granularity for forensic purposes
01:12 Tom Hayes: Yeah on logs we need detailed token-level traceability, we need to show who called what model, when, and from where - also retention windows and redaction policies
01:24 Samira Patel: Understood. For token-level traceability we typically surface per-request metadata, route/model, timestamp, and an anonymized request id; full payloads are only available in private/de-identified modes or via customer-managed private deployments. That's usually the distinction - hosted API has limited payload retention by default
01:44 Priya Sharma: Can you confirm SSO / RBAC options, we require SAML POC for our SSO provider and fine-grained roles for our auditors
01:54 Ari Chen: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC is role-based with admin/operator/audit roles, plus API keys. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own IdP and lock down access further
02:10 Tom Hayes: About KMS: does Redwood manage keys or do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KeyVault
02:18 Samira Patel: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we use our managed KMS but we have envelope encryption and can provide attestations. There's also an option to integrate HSM for enterprise contracts. We'll send a diagram showing key flow — basically we do envelope encryption, model caches are encrypted on disk, and the master key rotation schedule is documented in SOC2 artifacts
02:46 Rachel Nguyen: When you say envelope encryption, do you mean customer keys directly encrypt token cache or you do a double wrap? Need to explain for our audit
02:55 Samira Patel: It's a double-wrap pattern: request-level data is encrypted by ephemeral data key, that key is wrapped with the customer-managed master key where configured. In hosted environment master is Redwood-managed, but with Dedicated/Private the customer key is used. I'll include a simplified diagram in the evidence bundle
03:10 Tom Hayes: Okay good. Also please detail how KV cache is persisted — sometimes we see transcripts say "kay vee cache" which confuses auditors, but basically is the KV cache for model context
03:22 Ari Chen: Next on SOC 2 / ISO scoping — are you asking for a copy of our SOC 2 Type II and what about ISO 27001 scope
03:30 Rachel Nguyen: Yes SOC 2 Type II is required, plus clarity on if ISO is scoped to hosting services or also to the private deployment package
03:40 Samira Patel: Our SOC 2 Type II covers hosted API and the Redwood control plane; Dedicated capacity has overlapping controls and we have separate attestations for Dedicated customers under NDA. For Private/on-prem the customer is responsible for local controls but we provide the installation checklist and security hardening guide. For ISO, our cert covers the control plane and select hosted services — we'll share the ISO scope note
03:58 Priya Sharma: Procurement will need estimated delivery timeline for evidence to keep our review moving
04:05 Ari Chen: We're aiming to deliver initial SIG answers with SOC 2 and KMS diagrams within 3 business days — so by Monday the 6th, does that work
04:13 Rachel Nguyen: That works, though we'll likely ask follow-ups as we map items
04:18 Tom Hayes: One technical question: how do you capture audit logs for API calls — can Elmwood export syslog or pull via a log ingestion endpoint
04:28 Samira Patel: For Hosted we provide an audit log export in JSON lines via an S3 bucket or via our SIEM integration connectors (splunk/syslog). For Dedicated/Private you can ship logs to your syslog endpoint or we can forward to a customer-managed endpoint. We'll include a sample export with field mappings (timestamp, request_id, user_id, model, route, latency, bytes_in/out)
04:53 Rachel Nguyen: Do you redact PII from logs by default, or is that a per-config option
04:58 Samira Patel: By default hosted logs redact sensitive payload data; metadata remains. In Dedicated or Private you can choose to retain payloads or apply custom redaction rules — this is part of the deployment agreement
05:12 Tom Hayes: Regarding data residency: Elmwood needs EU region hosting for EU-labeled funds and a contractual clause for data residency plus proof we can route EU traffic to EU-only inference
05:25 Ari Chen: We have regional routing policies; you can pin customers to EU-only regions and we can provide contractual Data Residency Addendum. We'll show the routing config example and fallback policies — important for canary and burst capacity we might route temporarily to other zones if you allow failover
05:46 Rachel Nguyen: So if we pin to EU, can Redwood still perform model updates or are there constraints
05:52 Samira Patel: Updates can be staged in EU without leaving the region; model binaries are distributed to region-local serving pools. For certain third-party model artifacts there may be licensing constraints but we'll flag those in the SIG answers
06:10 Priya Sharma: On the evidence bundle, what format do you prefer? We export our questionnaires as XLSX
06:15 Ari Chen: XLSX is fine. We'll return a completed XLSX SIG/CAIQ and a zip with PDFs for SOC reports, diagrams, and exported logs. We'll also include a short README mapping controls to files
06:30 Tom Hayes: Can you provide a sample of your incident response timeline and encryption key rotation policy
06:36 Samira Patel: Yes, sample IR timeline and key rotation schedule will be included — note the IR runbooks are high-level in the bundle; detailed playbooks are shared under NDA
06:46 Rachel Nguyen: Also procurement will need the standard contract SLAs and liability language — can your legal team provide template redlines
06:52 Ari Chen: Yes procurement we'll add legal templates; however final redlines are part of enterprise negotiation — we'll include our standard terms
07:00 Priya Sharma: Timelinewise, after initial evidence we have a two week review window and a final procurement decision by end of month
07:07 Ari Chen: Ok sounds good. Let's talk about one edge—customer-managed keys in GCP KMS, do you have a sample IAM policy to grant wrap/unwrap to your service account
07:16 Samira Patel: We do. We'll include a sample minimum-privilege IAM policy and instructions for granting access. For Azure KeyVault we show RBAC roles and managed identities as well
07:28 Tom Hayes: For the audit logs sample can you include a mapping of fields to SIEM dashboards so our security team can validate quickly
07:35 Samira Patel: Yes that's part of the sample export, we'll add a dashboard mapping doc
07:42 Rachel Nguyen: Any blockers from Redwood side for delivering evidence within that 3 day window
07:48 Ari Chen: No blockers; Samira has the pull for the SOC/ISO notes and I'll assemble the SIG answers. We'll redact anything sensitive and push via secure share. We'll use our secure evidence room link and share access controls
07:58 Priya Sharma: One last point: do you have SOC2 coverage dates and SOC auditor details
08:03 Samira Patel: Yes we'll include the SOC2 Type II period and the auditor name and contact to the extent allowed
08:10 Rachel Nguyen: Great. If we need on-prem demo, we'll coordinate schedules, Tom will lead the technical deep dive
08:16 Tom Hayes: Sounds good
08:18 Ari Chen: Ok recap: Ari to send SIG answers and zip with SOC/ISO/KMS diagrams by 2026-12-06, Samira to share audit log sample and key management diagrams by 2026-12-04, coordinate on-prem demo if requested. Any final questions?
08:30 Rachel Nguyen: None from me, thank you
08:32 Priya Sharma: Thanks
08:33 Tom Hayes: Thanks

Action items (verbal recap):
- Ari: assemble and share SIG/CAIQ completed XLSX, SOC2 & ISO artifacts, legal templates (due 2026-12-06)
- Samira: sample audit logs, KMS diagrams, minimal-privilege IAM policies, IR timeline (due 2026-12-04)
- Rachel: share Elmwood residency policy doc for mapping (due 2026-12-08)

End of transcript.
